GET /v1/platform/.well-known/jwks.json.help: Every public key that may verify a live platform token.

GET /v1/platform/.well-known/openid-conf.help: Issuer metadata: where keys and the token endpoint are and what they support.

POST /v1/platform/token.help: Session tokens (login exchange; the CLI's device and refresh grants) and the `job` grant (form-encoded).

POST /v1/platform/revoke.help: Revoke a job token when its job ends or is cancelled, or sign a CLI login out (`token=<job token>` or `token=lr_…`, RFC 7009 form).

POST /v1/platform/login/code.help: Email a one-time sign-in code; `202` whether or not the email is known.

POST /v1/platform/login/code/verify.help: Sign in with the emailed code (a new email becomes a new user).

POST /v1/platform/login/password.help: Sign in with a password; an unverified email answers `403` and gets a code.

POST /v1/platform/signup.help: Create a password user; answers `403 email-verification-required` with the code sent.

POST /v1/platform/login/email-verificati.help: Finish a login held for email verification with the emailed code.

POST /v1/platform/login/password-reset.help: Email a reset link to `<app>/reset-password?token=…`; `202` whether or not the email is known.

POST /v1/platform/login/password-reset/c.help: Set a new password with the emailed token.

GET /v1/platform/login/social/{provider}.help: Where to send the browser for a social login (`google`); the provider returns to `redirect_uri` (registered in WorkOS) with `code` and `state`.

POST /v1/platform/login/social/callback.help: Finish a social login with the returned code.

POST /v1/platform/login/refresh.help: New AuthKit tokens for a live session; `401 login-refused` when it ended.

POST /v1/platform/device/code.help: Start the CLI's device flow (RFC 8628 §3.1; form-encoded, no client authentication).

GET /v1/platform/device/{user_code}.help: A waiting device authorization, for the person to confirm (platform session token).

POST /v1/platform/device/{user_code}/app.help: Approve a waiting code: the CLI's next poll signs it in as the caller.

POST /v1/platform/device/{user_code}/den.help: Deny a waiting code: the CLI's next poll answers `access_denied`.

GET /v1/platform/me.help: The caller and every tenant they belong to.

GET /v1/platform/tenants.help: The caller's tenants with their role.

POST /v1/platform/tenants.help: Create a tenant; the caller becomes its admin. Needs no membership: this is how a first-time user gets their workspace.

GET /v1/platform/tenants/{tenant_id}.help: A tenant the caller belongs to, with the caller's role.

GET /v1/platform/tenants/{tenant_id}/mem.help: Members of a tenant the caller belongs to.

POST /v1/platform/tenants/{tenant_id}/me.help: Add a signed-in user by email with a role template (`role`) or a custom scope set (`scopes`) you hold (admin).

GET /v1/platform/tenants/{tenant_id}/pri.help: Everyone the tenant's histories may name: current and former members, and API keys with their creators (any member).

PATCH /v1/platform/tenants/{tenant_id}/m.help: Change a member's role to a template (`role`) or a custom scope set (`scopes`) you hold (admin); the last admin cannot be demoted.

DELETE /v1/platform/tenants/{tenant_id}/.help: Remove a member (admin) or leave (self); the last admin cannot leave.

POST /v1/platform/tenants/{tenant_id}/ke.help: Issue an API key (admin): the response is the only time the key is shown.

GET /v1/platform/tenants/{tenant_id}/key.help: The tenant's API keys, newest first, revoked and expired ones included (admin).

DELETE /v1/platform/tenants/{tenant_id}/.help: Revoke an API key at once (admin); services refuse it within 60 s.

GET /v1/platform/revocations.help: Revoked job tokens and API keys not yet expired; public, and not cached on the way (services cache it ≤ 60 s).

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios.help: One page of the tenant's portfolios by id (only those in a `resources` claim, when the token has one), each with its display name and headline (policy 02 interfaces Rule 2.6): active and archived account counts, its newest sync job, and the open-item count and value a job stored when it last derived the portfolio's reads (`null` until one has; `value` is the net value in the reporting currency with `complete` and `valued_at`). Nothing is derived or valued on this read; `{P}/overview` and `{P}/valuation` are the current figures.

query.name: cursor
query.help: A previous page's `next_cursor`; pass the same filters again.

POST /v1/portfolio/portfolios.help: Create a portfolio with its policy and no accounts; `label` is its display name (default none: show the id), `policy.functional_currency` (the reporting currency: an `id` of `GET /currencies`, `usd` by default) and `policy.accrual` (`monthly` by default) are its settings.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: The portfolio's display name (`label`, null when none), its policy, every field with its default made explicit (`functional_currency`, `accrual`, `minor_unit`, …), and its active and archived account counts.

PATCH /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfoli.help: Rename (`label`: 1–100 characters, or null to show the id) and change policy fields (e.g. `{"functional_currency": "euro", "accrual": "yearly"}`), flat in one body; the others keep their values. `changes` lists every changed field. Nothing is recomputed in the request; a new reporting currency (an `id` of `GET /currencies`) has its USD rates fetched with the change (one small Terminal fetch: prices are stored in USD, so no asset is priced again). `effects` says what a policy change leaves stale (derived reads, the new currency's rates when their fetch failed (`fx`), evm accounts to re-sync for a new accrual schedule); a rename leaves nothing. A policy change queues a derive job (`derive_job`); reads serve the previous holdings and items until it finishes.

DELETE /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfol.help: Delete the portfolio's accounts, imports and books; the units' resources and revisions stay.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: One page of the accounts by id, with their label, archive time, resources, import status, source verification and coverage, and each one's `pnl` from the live books (policy 05 rule 44.4, decision 34): its live MTM P&L (`pnl`, its NAV now less its net transfers in, internal ones included, at market: `nav`, `contributions`) with its booked realized P&L, income and expenses as components and the rest `unrealized`, `pooled` under the `global` lot scope; null before the live books are computed.

query.name: archived
query.help: Only archived (true) or only active (false) accounts; both by default.

query.name: cursor
query.help: A previous page's `next_cursor`; pass the same filters again.

POST /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio.help: Add an account (and hl sub-accounts) with new unit resources: one per confirmed network for evm (or per active network when none are given), one otherwise. An existing resource is bound only when `resource_id` names it (for an evm account, `resources` names one per network), and one other accounts read only with `share: true` (else `409 resource-shared`; policy 04 Rule 13.7). Never syncs.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: One account with its resources, import status, source verification and coverage.

PATCH /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfoli.help: Rename (`label`), archive or restore (`archived`); the id never changes. Archiving or restoring queues a derive job (`derive_job`); reads serve the previous holdings and items until it finishes.

DELETE /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfol.help: Remove the account, its resource mapping and label; by default its unit resources are only unlinked. Imported data stays.

query.name: delete_resources
query.help: Also delete the unit resources through their units (evidence stays; a resource another account reads is kept).

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: Every import of the account, newest first: the `version`, `state_sha256` and `imported_at` of the state each copied (legacy revision imports: `revision_id`).

query.name: cursor
query.help: A previous page's `next_cursor`; pass the same filters again.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: Every active account's budgets in one read (policy 02 interfaces Rule 10.7): per resource its tenant budget (`limit`: `limit_usd`, the `period` it covers, `spent_usd` in that period, `remaining_usd`), and provider spend against the operator's caps and next-sync estimates (evm per network: Alchemy/dRPC this month; hl: the S3 archive over the resource's life), per account and in total. One read per unit, no provider call; `would_exceed` says a sync would pass a resource's limit, which its unit then refuses (a hard limit, policy 02 access Rule 7.2). The units are read with the caller's own credential.

The account's resources with their tenant budgets (`limit`) and their units' usage reads (`spend` against the operator's caps, `estimate`, `would_exceed`), and the total; cex and dydx resources have none. A unit that cannot answer leaves an `error` on its resources; the units are read with the caller's own credential.

POST /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio.help: Diff the body's accounts and policy against the portfolio, then bind resources and store them (`litmus-dev apply`).

query.name: dry_run
query.help: Return the plan only.

query.name: prune
query.help: Delete stored accounts the body omits.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: One page of imported records in `(time, id)` order (500 by default, at most 5,000), with each account's coverage; follow `next_cursor` with the same filters.

query.name: account
query.help: Only this account.

query.name: from
query.help: RFC 3339, inclusive.

query.name: to
query.help: RFC 3339, exclusive.

query.name: type
query.help: Record type.

query.name: cursor
query.help: A previous page's `next_cursor`; pass the same filters again.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: Balances per compartment from translated legs up to `at` (`state`); with `valued`, prices, values and totals that never count a gap as zero.

query.name: account
query.help: Only this account.

query.name: at
query.help: ISO 8601 instant.

query.name: valued
query.help: Price and value every balance in the reporting currency, with totals (stored prices only: latest without `at`, else daily).

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: Missing prices: one page of the daily ones of the last fill (`POST {P}/prices`) by asset and day, most lookups first (`daily_total` counts them all), and every held asset without a usable latest price.

query.name: cursor
query.help: A previous page's `next_cursor`; pass the same filters again.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: The counts of every matching open item by kind (`total`, `counts`), and one page of the items by id, each with its resolve hint; follow `next_cursor` with the same filters. Per-account counts for every account at once are in `GET {P}/overview`.

query.name: account
query.help: Only this account.

query.name: kind
query.help: Item kind.

query.name: cursor
query.help: A previous page's `next_cursor`; pass the same filters again.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: The portfolio at a glance, in one call: every account with its unit resources (each with the version, state digest, record count and time of its last import, and that import's verification summary `{status, verified_at, failed}` in policy 03 contract rule 2.6.1's shape), its open items counted by kind, its resources counted by verification status (`none`: without one), and its newest sync job; then the same counts for the whole portfolio, and its newest sync job.

query.name: archived
query.help: Only archived (true) or only active (false) accounts; both by default.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: The portfolio's value in the reporting currency, in one call: the total and every active account's, each split into `assets` (valued holdings), `debt` (valued liabilities, zero or negative) and `value` (net assets = assets + debt), with counts of valued holdings, gaps and holdings not valued by design, `mostly_unvalued`, and each account's `share` of the net total; then the portfolio's price gaps counted by reason, and `complete`.

query.name: at
query.help: ISO 8601 instant: value at it with daily prices. Default: the current holdings at the latest prices.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: One page of the portfolio's corrections in force in application order, each with who recorded it, when, in which job, the AI-made mark when an agent's API key made it, and the links it owns. A withdrawn correction is not kept (policy 05 sub-ledger Rule 3.7).

query.name: withdrawn
query.help: `true` lists none: a withdrawn correction is deleted, with no history (policy 01 portfolio Rule 7.3); `false` or absent lists those in force.

query.name: cursor
query.help: A previous page's `next_cursor`; pass the same filters again.

POST /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio.help: Queue a correction job that applies the correction, recorded with the token's subject, the time and the job, or previews it (`?dry_run=true`, which needs only `read`); poll `GET /jobs/{id}`, whose `result` is the `CorrectionResult`. `merge_internal` links a withdrawal and a deposit as one internal movement; `classify_boundary` tags an unlinked transfer as a boundary transfer with the counterparty on the other side (policy 05 sub-ledger Rule 3.3): an id from `GET {P}/counterparties`, or `{label, mine, note?, reference?}`, created in the same job; `replaces` withdraws that tag of the same record in the same job. Its counterparty's flag decides the booking (Rule 2): someone else, at market value both ways; mine, out at cost and in at market value as the new cost; never income or expense. `ownership_retained` is derived from the flag, and one that disagrees is a 422. The correction records the token's subject, the job and, for an agent's API key, the AI-made mark. The result's `effect` lists the records concerned (before/after: `link`, `classified`, `unmatched`), the links added, the open items resolved, added or changed, and the balances that move. The records are checked before the job is queued, and again by the job: they must be unlinked, unclassified transfers (404 `record-not-found` or `counterparty-not-found`, 409 `correction-conflict`, 422 otherwise). An identical request of the same user joins the job already queued or running.

query.name: dry_run
query.help: Preview only: the effect of applying it, from a scratch derivation; nothing is written.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: One page of the unlinked transfers, oldest first: the active accounts' transfer-like records that no link and no `classify_boundary` covers (what `unmatched_transfer` items count, and unsolicited receipts, flagged). `total` counts every one. Their ids are what corrections take; `GET {P}/unmatched` shows each beside its nearest counterparts.

query.name: account
query.help: Only this account.

query.name: asset
query.help: Only this asset id (or unit symbol).

query.name: cursor
query.help: A previous page's `next_cursor`; pass the same filters again.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: One correction in force; 404 once withdrawn.

DELETE /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfol.help: Queue a correction job that withdraws a correction: it is deleted with the links it owns, and no record of it, or of who withdrew it, is kept (policy 01 portfolio Rule 7.3); or previews that (`?dry_run=true`, which needs only `read`). Poll `GET /jobs/{id}` for the `CorrectionResult` (the correction as it was) with its `effect`. 404 `correction-not-found` when no such correction is in force, before anything is queued.

query.name: dry_run
query.help: Preview only: the effect of applying it, from a scratch derivation; nothing is written.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: The portfolio's counterparties by label, each with the transfers it tags (`tags`) and what they moved per asset, in minus out (`quantities`). A counterparty is custom, current state only, and never identified by address (Rule 3.1).

POST /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio.help: Create a counterparty `{label, mine, note?, reference?}`: `mine` when the asset stays the owner's in an account Litmus does not track yet, else someone else (Rule 3.1). Its `id` is a slug of the label (`Marcel (loan)` → `marcel-loan`), fixed once created; it records who created it. A tag can also create one (`POST {P}/corrections`).

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: One counterparty with the transfers it tags; 404 `counterparty-not-found`.

PATCH /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfoli.help: Change `label`, `mine`, `note` or `reference` in place, with no version kept (Rule 3.1.5). A flag change rebooks every transfer it tags (Rule 3.2): their tags follow it, and when it tags any, a derive job is queued (`derive_job`); reads serve the previous items until it finishes.

DELETE /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfol.help: Queue a correction job that deletes the counterparty and withdraws every tag that names it, so those transfers are untagged again (Rule 3.1.6); nothing of it is kept (Rule 3.7). With `?dry_run=true` (which needs only `read`) the job lists the tags it would withdraw and their effect, and writes nothing. Poll `GET /jobs/{id}`: its `result` is `{dry_run, counterparty, withdrawn, effect}`. 404 `counterparty-not-found` before anything is queued.

query.name: dry_run
query.help: Preview only: list the tags it would withdraw and their effect; nothing is written.

POST /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio.help: Queue a reconciliation: every unlinked transfer-like record is matched again by policy 01's passes, links whose record disappeared are pruned (a correction that owned one becomes a `failed_correction` item), links made by corrections or by the units' adapters are kept, and the derived holdings and open items are refreshed. The result counts links, candidates, unmatched and pruned, per pass. A reconciliation already queued or running is returned instead. Needs `sync`.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: One page of links by id: each pair of records portfolio treats as one internal movement, with both records (account, time, legs, the on-chain `reference`, the unit resource and the evidence digests to open at the unit), its kind, the pass or correction that made it, and the residual (`deposit + withdrawal`: a fee or loss in transit) when both sides move one asset. A side whose record is gone is null (a dangling link, pruned by the next reconciliation).

query.name: account
query.help: Only links with a side in this account.

query.name: kind
query.help: Only this kind.

query.name: source
query.help: Only links a reconciliation pass (`reconcile`), a unit adapter (`adapter`) or a correction (`correction`) made.

query.name: cursor
query.help: A previous page's `next_cursor`; pass the same filters again.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: One link with both of its records.

One page of the unmatched transfer legs (the records `unmatched_transfer` items count), oldest first, each beside its `nearest` counterparts: unlinked transfer-like records of the same asset and the opposite direction in any account, fewest reasons first, then nearest in time, each with why it did not link at the loosest rung of reconciliation (`same_resource`: both from one resource, such as one network of an evm account; `type`, `unresolved_asset`, `network`, `tx_id`, `amount`: above what was sent or more than 5% below it, `window`: more than 30 days after, or more than 1 hour before; `ambiguous`: every rule accepts the pair, but other candidates competed, so reconciliation left both). No reasons means a reconciliation would link them now (records synced since the last one). Unsolicited receipts are never legs, only counterparts. Resolve a leg with a correction (`POST {P}/corrections`).

query.name: account
query.help: Only legs of this account.

query.name: asset
query.help: Only legs of this asset (catalogue id or the unit's name).

query.name: nearest
query.help: Counterparts to show beside each leg.

query.name: cursor
query.help: A previous page's `next_cursor`; pass the same filters again.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: One page of the portfolio's history, one row per transaction (policy 02 interfaces Rule 2.4.1): a linked withdrawal and deposit as one `transfer` row with both records (withdrawal first), the link and the residual (the fee or loss in transit) when both move one asset; else the records of one account's transaction (`event`, its records sharing a `tx_id`). The records paying the transaction's network fee are the row's `fee` (records, legs per asset, value), a row of their own (`fee`) only when their transaction moved nothing else. Each row carries its `value` in the reporting currency (`currency`) at the daily prices of its UTC day, `complete` false with the unpriced assets when a leg has none; the counterparty a boundary tag in force names on one of its records; and whether a transfer leg is `unmatched` (see `GET {P}/unmatched`). Each record carries its account, time, legs, the on-chain `reference`, its unit resource and evidence digests to open at the unit. A row appears once, where its first record passing the filters falls, so filtering by one account still shows the other account's side; a fee's records match the filters only on a row of their own. `total` counts the rows matching the filters and `facets` the rows each account, type and asset would match with the other filters, the same on every page.

query.name: account
query.help: Only rows with a record of this account.

query.name: asset
query.help: Only rows with a record moving this asset (catalogue id or the unit's name).

query.name: type
query.help: Only rows with a record of one of these event types (repeatable).

query.name: from
query.help: RFC 3339, inclusive.

query.name: to
query.help: RFC 3339, exclusive.

query.name: order
query.help: `desc`: newest first.

query.name: cursor
query.help: A previous page's `next_cursor`; pass the same filters again.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: The cross-account audit, computed on request from the imported ledger (no unit or provider call): unmatched transfer-like records by account, type and asset; every link's conservation (what the withdrawal sent against what the deposit received, with tolerated differences by asset) and dangling links; the per-account state checks of the translated legs against the units' checkpoints; the units' open source items; and `passed`. It translates the whole ledger, so it takes seconds on a large portfolio.

query.name: latest_only
query.help: Check only the latest checkpoint per account.

query.name: verbose
query.help: Keep passed state checks in the report.

POST /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio.help: Seal the books at `as_of` (default: the end of the latest import) for a `reason` (policy 05 rule 37.2): `export`, `final` (needs `admin`; the revision is then marked final, rule 37.3) or `snapshot`. Nothing seals automatically. When a revision under the current policy with the same `as_of` and input digest exists, it is reused: answered at once (200, `reused`) when the live books at that `as_of` are cached and current, else found by the seal job once it has translated and priced, before it runs anything else. Otherwise the job translates the ledger up to `as_of`, fetches the daily prices its events need (never prices of holdings, rule 1.5), validates, runs the engine, audits, and seals the package (records, links, policy, coverage, corrections, the prices the events used, engine input and output with its rows and open-lot rows, audit, and every cited evidence object fetched from its unit; no series and no valuation, rule 23.5) as a new immutable revision recording its reason and input digest; its progress names each step, packaging and storing included. The result is the books summary with its `revision_id`, `reason` and `reused`. A person's run holds one job token for reading evidence from the units, revoked when it ends; a run started with an API key reads with that key (403 `key-audience-missing` when its audience lacks a unit). A seal at the same `as_of` already queued or running is returned instead. Needs `correct` (`admin` for `final`).

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: One page of the sealed books revisions, newest first: each one's status (`final`, `draft`, or `stale` when built under another policy than the portfolio's), `as_of`, policy, completeness and verification by account, when and by whom it was sealed, in which job, the imports it booked and its file count. `active` marks the newest.

query.name: cursor
query.help: A previous page's `next_cursor`; pass the same filters again.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: The live books' state (policy 05 term 18, rule 36): the portfolio's books computed in memory from its current inputs under its current policy, whenever an input changes, and never sealed. It says their `as_of` (the end of the latest import, or the instant asked for), input digest, when they were computed, whether they are `updating` (their inputs changed since: a live job is computing them again, and every read serves these meanwhile), their completeness, open issues, warnings and audit. They are labelled `live`, never books, draft or final. Their rows are `GET {P}/books/live/rows?kind=`, their realized series `GET {P}/books/live/series`, and every accounting read takes `revision=live` by default. 202 with the live job that computes them when none are computed at that `as_of` yet; seal them with `POST {P}/books`. Needs `read`.

query.name: as_of
query.help: The books at this instant (Close & export's date, policy 05 rule 37.1.4); default: at the end of the latest import.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: One sealed revision: its listing fields, its books summary as sealed (records, links, translation, engine completeness and exceptions, open positions, realized P&L by account, compartment and instrument, flows, pricing, audit) and its package files with their SHA-256.

One page of a revision's rows of one kind as the engine sealed them (policy 05 rule 36): disposals with their lots, proceeds, cost and P&L; income and expenses by nature label (a perpetual's realized P&L names its `instrument`); holdings (per lot key, with opaque positions and open perp positions) and liabilities: the open-lot rows at `as_of` (`kind`, `quantity`, remaining `cost`, a position's entry basis in `settles_in`; policy 05 term 14), each with its live `value`, `label`, `price_at` and `unrealized` P&L (value − remaining cost) joined on read at `as_of` (rule 39.12.2; null when not valued), `values` saying when they were computed, and `warning` when the books' total P&L at `as_of` differs from the live MTM P&L (rule 39.5.2); the journal's double-entry lines; the movements with outside parties (policy 05 sub-ledger Rule 7): one row per boundary transfer leg (date, account, compartment, asset, quantity, direction, value, basis `market` or `carried`, cost and realized gain or loss when out, counterparty or untagged with its flag, note, reference, correction id, who tagged it, record id), untagged first, with `counterparties`: each one's transfers, value in and out and balance at `as_of`, the untagged first as their subtotal. Decimals are text; every row but a journal line has its `account`. `revision_id` may be `live`: the live books' rows (policy 05 term 18; 409 `live-books-missing` before they are computed, and a live job is queued when they are missing or behind). 409 `rows-unavailable` for a revision sealed before revisions carried rows (for `boundary`, before they carried its movements with outside parties).

query.name: kind
query.help: `disposals` (realized rows), `income` (income and expenses), `holdings` and `liabilities` at `as_of`, `journal`, or `boundary` (movements with outside parties).

query.name: cursor
query.help: A previous page's `next_cursor`; pass the same filters again.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: A revision's realized series (policy 05 rules 36 and 39.7), computed on read from its sealed rows: at every UTC day end (or the last of each month) from its first booked row to its `as_of`, then `as_of`, its realized P&L, its income and expenses by nature label, and their total (realized P&L + income − expenses), each in the interval (`period`) and to its end (`cumulative`). It carries no value, cost or unrealized P&L: NAV and MTM P&L are the live `{P}/totals`, which with `revision` adds unrealized P&L over time. `revision_id` may be `current`, or `live` for the live books (policy 05 term 18; their realized amounts per UTC day). 409 `rows-unavailable` for a revision sealed without rows or without an `as_of`.

query.name: interval
query.help: Every UTC day end, or the last point of each month.

query.name: from
query.help: The first instant served.

query.name: to
query.help: The last instant served.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: A sealed revision's export (policy 05 rule 31). `package`: the sealed package as a zip file, every artifact at its package path, each verified against its hash when read; `manifest.json` lists the files with their SHA-256; unzip it and run a replay offline, or `POST …/replay` to replay it here. `summary` (rule 31.5): the accountant's summary, one XLSX workbook dated in the portfolio's time zone: Summary (the header of rule 32.1, NAV at the period's start and end, net contributions, P&L and its breakdown), P&L by month and account, P&L by asset, Balance at cost (open-lot rows at `as_of` with market value and unrealized P&L when exported), Journal entries by month and account, Disposals, Income and expenses, and Open issues and notes. `live` is a 409: seal first (`POST {P}/books {reason: export}`).

query.name: format
query.help: `package` (the sealed package as a zip) or `summary` (the accountant's summary, an XLSX workbook).

query.name: from
query.help: `summary`: the period's first instant; default: after the newest earlier final revision, else the first record.

query.name: to
query.help: `summary`: the period's last instant; default: `as_of`.

POST /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio.help: Queue a replay of a sealed revision: verify every file of its package against the manifest and the records' evidence closure, check the pinned engine is the installed one, rebuild the engine input from the pinned records, links and policy, run the engine again, and check its rows files. No unit or provider is called and nothing changes. The result says whether the books `matched` and how many files were verified. A replay of the same revision already queued or running is returned instead. Needs `read` (policy 05 rule 36: a check that changes nothing).

Mark a revision final for its `as_of` (policy 05 rule 26): the books the portfolio stands behind for that date, replacing the revision that was final for it (both stay). Open issues (`GET {P}/books/{rev}`'s `issues`: price gaps, engine exceptions, unbooked records, series points not valued, `failed` and `unassessable` coverage) never forbid it and need no acknowledgement; any given are recorded with their reason and count, and one that names no open issue is a 422. The mark records who made it and when, and states the revision's open-issue count (`open_issues`). A revision sealed without an `as_of` cannot be final (422). Needs `admin`.

DELETE /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfol.help: Unmark a final revision: its `as_of` has no final books until another is marked. 404 when it is not final. Needs `admin`.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: The live layer's headline figures (policy 05 rules 36 and 39.1), without books: at every UTC day end (or the last of each month) from `from` to `to`, live NAV (holdings and opaque compartments valued, net of liabilities, plus open positions' unrealized P&L at the mark), net contributions (boundary transfers at their market value) and MTM P&L = NAV − contributions, each point `complete` or listing the assets not valued (`missing`; never valued at zero). Joined with the live books by default (`revision=live`, rule 36; a sealed revision when named), each point they cover adds its realized results to date (`realized`: realized P&L + income − expenses) and `unrealized` = MTM P&L − realized (rule 39.12.1): the live books cover every point, since nothing after the latest import is known, and are valued at the time of reading (decision 33); a sealed revision covers the points up to its `as_of`, which is a point too. `revision` states the basis (rule 34): its id, `as_of`, policy, `valued_at`, and for the live books `updating` (a live job is computing them again) or `computed: false` (not computed yet: no point carries realized results, and a live job is queued). `warning` states why the books' total P&L at `as_of` (realized + per-holding unrealized) differs from the live MTM P&L, by cause (rule 39.5.2); it is never folded into unrealized P&L. Values are computed when read and may change with prices or valuation rules (`computed_at`). 404 for an unknown revision (or none under the current policy for `current`); 409 `rows-unavailable` for one sealed without rows.

query.name: interval
query.help: Every UTC day end, or the last day end of each month.

query.name: from
query.help: The first instant served.

query.name: to
query.help: The last instant served.

query.name: revision
query.help: The books to join: `live` (the default: the live books, policy 05 term 18), a sealed revision, or `current` (the newest sealed under the current policy); their realized results and unrealized P&L for the instants they cover, and the warning at their `as_of`.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: The live layer per account, compartment and asset (policy 05 rule 39.2), without books: at every UTC day end (or the last of each month) from `from` to `to`, each holding, liability (negative), open perp position (its unrealized P&L at the mark) and opaque compartment (one position valued from its event-implied contents, at least zero) with its quantity, value in the reporting currency and one valuation label (`market`, `stale`, `peg`, `first_available`, `components`, `components_stale`, `opaque_estimate`; none when not valued), and the point's NAV, net contributions, MTM P&L and completeness. Narrow it with `from`, `to` and `interval`: a year of daily points is large.

query.name: interval
query.help: Every UTC day end, or the last day end of each month.

query.name: from
query.help: The first instant served.

query.name: to
query.help: The last instant served.

GET /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio_.help: P&L by asset, account, month or year (policy 05 rules 36, 43.2 and 44.5), from the live books by default (or a sealed revision), with the portfolio's `total`: P&L now and its breakdown, whose lines add up to it. Each group carries realized P&L, income and expenses (with `flows` by label), unrealized P&L, `not_in_books` and P&L. An asset group adds the remaining `cost` of its holdings, valued now for the live books (decision 33). An account group's P&L is its live MTM P&L (`nav` − `contributions`), its booked figures components and the rest unrealized, `pooled` under the `global` lot scope (decision 34). A month or year group is dated in the portfolio's `time_zone`; its P&L is the MTM P&L at its end less at its start, its booked figures those of the period and its unrealized P&L the change over it. `from` and `to` narrow the booked figures to those days. `basis` states the books and when holdings are valued (rule 34). 409 `live-books-missing` before the live books are computed (a live job is queued). Needs `read`.

query.name: by
query.help: `asset`, `account`, or `month` / `year` in the portfolio time zone.

query.name: from
query.help: The first instant served.

query.name: to
query.help: The last instant served.

query.name: revision
query.help: The books: `live` (the default, the live books) or a sealed revision.

POST /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio.help: Queue a sync of the given accounts, else of every active one (archived accounts never sync): per resource a unit sync (a child job), then the import, then a reconcile of the whole portfolio (policy 01 portfolio Rule 10; its summary, or its error, is the result's `reconcile`); a sync already queued or running for the portfolio is returned instead. The job's `accounts` are fixed now (every active account, for a sync of all).

query.name: account
query.help: Only these accounts (repeatable); overrides the body.

POST /v1/portfolio/portfolios/{portfolio.help: Queue a rebuild of the whole ledger, a sync job of every active account (`request.rebuild`) that replaces the ledger instead of each account's records: the upgrade step after the units' records move to a new schema generation, which an account-by-account import refuses to mix.

Queue a price job: first the latest USD prices of held assets and the fiat rates (what current valuation reads, as a sync's end refreshes them), then a daily fill of every priced (asset, day) of the ledger and the reporting currency's daily rates from the Terminal API, gaps recorded (`GET {P}/prices/gaps`); a job already queued or running is returned instead. Its result is the fill report with `latest`, the latest refresh's report.

GET /v1/portfolio/jobs.help: One page of the tenant's portfolio jobs, newest first, each with its accounts, latest progress message, children (each with its latest step) and `dry_run` mark. `?portfolio=P&account=a&status=queued,running` finds an account's active sync; `?kind=books&status=succeeded` the last books run (policy 02 interfaces Rule 15).

query.name: portfolio
query.help: Only this portfolio.

query.name: status
query.help: Only jobs in these statuses: repeatable or comma-separated (`queued,running`).

query.name: kind
query.help: Only jobs of these kinds: repeatable or comma-separated (`sync,books`).

query.name: account
query.help: Only jobs covering this account (its `accounts`); requires `portfolio`, as account ids are per portfolio.

query.name: cursor
query.help: A previous page's `next_cursor`; pass the same filters again.

GET /v1/portfolio/jobs/{job_id}.help: One job with its complete progress, its unit child jobs (each with its latest step, times and record count), its `dry_run` mark, and its result or error once finished (policy 02 interfaces Rule 15).

POST /v1/portfolio/jobs/{job_id}/cancel.help: Cancel a queued or running job: its unfinished unit jobs are cancelled, its job token revoked, and nothing more is imported (accounts imported before stay). The portfolio's next sync can start at once. 409 when the job already succeeded or failed.

GET /v1/portfolio/currencies.help: The reporting currencies `policy.functional_currency` accepts, by ISO code: `{id, code, name}` per catalogue fiat currency Terminal serves a daily USD series for (`usd` and `euro` always). `id` is what the policy takes. Terminal is asked at most daily per process; when it cannot answer, every catalogue fiat currency is listed.

Empty when no portfolio uses the resource; the resource itself is its unit's (`GET /v1/<unit>/resources/{r}`).
